title: 4 pressure tactics scammers use to hijack your judgement
description: Social engineering attacks the person, not the device. Learn four pressure tactics in scam messages and the simple habit that beats them.

scenes.big: Scammers don't hack you. They hurry you.
scenes.say: Most scams don't break your device. They break your judgement, using pressure. There are four tactics to know.

The National Cyber Security Centre lists them. Authority: the message claims to be from someone official, like your bank or the tax office. Urgency: you're given a deadline. Emotion: it tries to make you panic, or get excited. Scarcity: the offer is nearly gone.

scenes.sub: the pressure is the red flag
scenes.say: Notice what they share. They all want you to act before you think. So the pressure itself is your warning sign.
If in doubt, don't reply. Hang up, then contact the organisation using a number you already trust, not the one in the message.
Got a scam text? Forward it to seven seven two six. Got a scam email? Send it to report at phishing dot gov dot UK. Follow, and stay one step ahead.
